summary: Build advanced community relations and social licence to operate capability with practical tools, frameworks, and dashboards. Enrol your team today.
lede: Community relations training helps senior practitioners and leaders responsible for affected-community relationships assess social risks and inform operational decisions. It covers stakeholder mapping and risk registers, engagement planning, and grievance intake and response workflows. Participants also learn to track social performance indicators and present findings through management dashboards.
audienceIntro: This advanced community relations and social licence to operate training is designed for senior practitioners and leaders who carry direct responsibility for relationships with affected communities and social stakeholders, and who must translate social risk into operational decisions and executive reporting.
modules: Community Relations and Social Licence Foundations
Stakeholder Mapping and Social Risk Analysis
Applying IFC Performance Standards and UNGPs
Designing Stakeholder Engagement and Consultation Plans
Grievance Redress Mechanisms and Incident Management
Digital Monitoring and Social Performance Dashboards
Integrating Social Licence into Strategy and Reporting
prerequisites: This is an advanced-level program designed for experienced practitioners. You should have at least 5 years of experience in community engagement, ESG, social performance, corporate affairs, or related project leadership roles. Familiarity with basic stakeholder engagement concepts, impact assessment processes, and corporate governance is expected. No coding is required, but you should be comfortable working with spreadsheets, simple dashboards, and digital collaboration tools. Advanced concepts such as ESG integration, human rights due diligence, and complex benefit-sharing agreements are taught at operational application and hands-on implementation levels, not at technical legal drafting depth.
